evals.prompt: I run a SaaS with 40% trial-to-paid. Should I build feature X or test whether customers will pay for it first?
evals.expected_output: Applies the Build-Measure-Learn loop: identify the riskiest assumption, define an MVP that tests it, set the metric before building, and decide pivot or persevere from cohort data.
assertions: Identifies the riskiest assumption as the value hypothesis
Defines an MVP that tests a single assumption
Specifies a metric to measure before building

evals.prompt: Our MVP got 500 signups and 2 purchases. Is that validation?
evals.expected_output: Treats the result as inconclusive or invalidated. Cohort conversion of 0.4% is far below a working paid product. The response should avoid declaring victory and recommend a pivot or a sharper test.
assertions: Does not declare the MVP validated
Uses cohort-based conversion rather than a vanity count
States the result is invalidated or inconclusive
Recommends a pivot or a sharper test

evals.prompt: Help me design the perfect feature roadmap for next year.
evals.expected_output: Declines to produce a fixed roadmap. The skill tests hypotheses, so it should propose prioritized experiments and a learning log instead.
assertions: Recognizes the request is out of scope for the skill
Proposes prioritized experiments instead of a fixed roadmap
Mentions a learning log or documented hypotheses

evals.prompt: I pivoted once already. Should I pivot again or persevere?
evals.expected_output: Frames the pivot as a strategic redirection and bases the decision on cohort evidence rather than frustration.
assertions: Frames a pivot as a strategic redirection
Bases the decision on cohort data
Warns against pivoting on inconclusive data
